issue.title: Broken tests on Python 3.7+ (urllib.parse behavior has changed)

summary.text: The verifier reproduced the bug, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after it, and found no regressions, no breaking inputs from Break My Fix, and no integrity issues. The guard stage ended as not_guarded and the mutation threshold for L2 was not met, so the most important next step is to strengthen the tests so they catch mutants of the fixed CONNECT host/port parsing.

survivors.description: Appends a trailing slash to the CONNECT URL, which changes the path and the built URL.
survivors.diff:
--- a/proxy/http/parser.py
+++ b/proxy/http/parser.py
@@ -111,3 +111,3 @@
             # Parse as //hostname:port to make it a valid URL for urlparse
-            self.url = urlparse.urlsplit(b'//' + url)
+            self.url = urlparse.urlsplit(b'//' + url + b'/')
         else:
survivors.words: proxy/http/parser.py:112: changing `self.url = urlparse.urlsplit(b'//' + url)` to `self.url = urlparse.urlsplit(b'//' + url + b'/')` made no test fail; no input tried behaved differently from the fix (it may be equivalent)

survivors.replacement: self.host, self.port = self.url.hostname, self.url.port or DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT
survivors.description: CONNECT without a port gets the default HTTP port instead of None.
survivors.diff:
--- a/proxy/http/parser.py
+++ b/proxy/http/parser.py
